limits: The current Valkyrie catalogue contains every type-compatible source affix, before rank/quality filtering. A rejected affix is not a separate missing mechanic; several rows can share one code.

Most numeric/range/scaled effects already have named-item paths. Ordinary rolls bypass those templates/aliases/ranges; NamedGear.ActiveProperties also requires a named-item identity and player wearer. Removing the ordinary whitelist alone would yield missing or incorrect effects.

Named registrations for skill/skilltab remain parameter-dependent; current consumers are predominantly player-specific. NPC inheritance, weapon-local versus global stats, proc ownership and save behavior require dedicated adapters and verification.

Last verified named-item gates are retained as historical runtime evidence, not a fresh certificate for the in-progress working tree. Some gates reflect unimplemented class/item replacement paths or unresolved source definitions, not missing general damage systems.
Approved exclusions, including charms, remain intentional and must not be turned into new feature requirements.
implementationOrder: Connect one shared property representation/alias/range/level-scaled resolver to ordinary and named gear, with existing numeric/save compatibility; keep unsupported events explicit.

Implement complete source-quality affix/property rolling and actual NPC equipment stat consumers, reusing the shared combat/resource/skill systems. Do not filter out unsupported source rolls or use player-only effects as NPC proof.

After the relevant class mechanics are ready, return to the deferred skill-effect list: skill-event dispatch, charges, oskills/item auras and remaining newer properties, using the relevant class handlers and exact ownership/resource/target/trigger rules. Individually uncertain mechanics remain recorded while unaffected work continues.

Verify real ordinary magic/rare and named items plus NPC equipment through damage/resources/skills/events and two save/reload cycles. Refresh acquisition eligibility only after its consumer checks pass.

userDecision: Keep skill-dependent item effects on a return list and implement them after the relevant class skills. Numeric/range/utility property integration remains active dependency work. No unavailable item or unfinished skill is enabled by listing it.
